changes.summary: include Beads and BV in portable task guidance
changes.body:
`beeswax prime` now includes `br` and `bv` by default. Shared guidance covers tracker identity, system-record filtering, task authority, claims, human reservations, verification and publication checkpoints. Tool-row filters retain this safety baseline. Prime works offline without a source checkout, tracker or installed skill. Release-history pointers remain limited to Hive-owned CLIs.

Optional: read `beeswax prime --help` for defaults and filters. Consolidate repeated safety guidance around one primer loading route while retaining repository-specific policy.

changes.summary: install a customizable Hive workflow during setup
changes.body:
Setup offers `--install-workflow-skill` and a default-off wizard choice. It installs only the public `hive` skill for selected Claude Code, Codex or Pi harnesses through `skills@1.7.2`. Installation requires Node >=22.20.0, npm/npx and network access; prime remains offline.

Existing skill destinations stop setup before writes. Installation runs last; failures retain completed setup phases and installer diagnostics for review of partial effects. The opt-in is not saved. Prime, hooks, sync and update never install or refresh the skill.

Optional: read `beeswax setup --help` before adding the flag to an intended setup invocation; `--yes` alone does not opt in. Omit the flag to preserve an existing workflow. Customize and commit installed files, selected links and installer metadata, then verify discovery and trust in each execution checkout. Review upstream replacements manually: the public main-branch skill evolves independently of the executable. Codex and Pi share its canonical project directory.

changes.summary: omit unavailable tools from update history pointers
changes.body:
`beeswax update` returns history commands only for known Hive tool names
found on `PATH`, including Waggle when present. It checks executable names,
not tool versions or supported subcommands.

After upgrading Hive's executables, refresh the project contract and follow
the returned history commands:

```sh
beeswax update --yes
```

The previous project version remains the exclusive `--since` baseline;
same-version updates point to current history without `--since`. This fix
requires no manual migration. Updating the contract does not install binaries
or apply or acknowledge adoption actions.

changes.summary: link project updates to offline tool histories
changes.body:
Use `beeswax changelog` to read bundled release changes and adoption
instructions. After upgrading, run `beeswax update --yes` in each adopting
project to refresh its saved contract and onboarding. The update reports
the previous and installed versions, with `<tool> changelog --since VERSION`
commands using the previous project version. Same-version updates point
to the current history without `--since`. Prime also directs agents to
changelogs after upgrades.

Updating the project lock does not apply or acknowledge adoption actions.

adoption.text: Review the tool histories linked by beeswax update for changes and adoption actions relevant to the project.

changes.summary: Setup reports configured artifacts, pending readiness checks and completed phases after partial failures.
